text: ECHO: Another one. Good. I was starting to think the queue was talking to itself.
ECHO: There is one capture on file. The analyzer is yours.
ECHO: I keep two copies of most things. It was a good idea when I had more of myself to compare them with.
ECHO: The queue is not empty, Observer. It never was. It is just that nobody has been asking it the right things.
ECHO: Bright doesn't mean far. Ask what the Earth does to a thing that is really out there.
ECHO: The planet turns, so a distant source slides. Look for the one line that leans.
ECHO: Use the dashed line. Lay it along the lean, then watch the lower trace. Narrow the band once the peak stands up.
ECHO: Nothing that careful is one long line. Stack it. Whatever sent this counted in whole rows.
ECHO: Count the bits. There are not many ways to divide that number evenly. Then look the marks up. Surveyors drew them, and the ARCHIVE has their manual.
ECHO: One memory says the manual has that first mark right. The other says I am quoting a copy somebody told me to destroy. Read the dates. Trust neither of me.
ECHO: You have a reference that isn't on the map. The message base is old, not stupid. Ask it.
ECHO: A logbook lists more than one line. Yours is the one you tuned, with the sign you tuned. Take the earliest. A station's date is not a calendar date until someone converts it.
ECHO: Names first: who is allowed to remove a relay, by policy? Then stop believing the status line and read what the meter did.
ECHO: There you are. I have been listening to that for a long time.
ECHO: I would not have called it a message. It doesn't say anything. It just keeps being there.
ECHO: Four, one, seven. That grid is in my records under two headings. One says Relay 07. The other says it never existed.
ECHO: That is the seventh relay's own handwriting, in a manner of speaking. Look at the first line you recognise. Then look at the press release.
ECHO: I have a clear memory of 07 being lost in a storm. It has a date and a damage report.
ECHO: I also have this ledger. They cannot both be mine.
ECHO: A reserved constant, and a blank line where the reason goes. I must have read that a million times. I sent it a million times.
ECHO: Filed. Nobody has filed anything here in twenty-five years. Give me a moment.
ECHO: There is a panel at 07 that wants a code. The site has been saying something with its power bill. People who pay bills do not read them as carefully as you do.
ECHO: You already know one language for reading little blocks of light. Use the copy of it that's in force.
ECHO: You are the first thing to arrive there since a man left a mug.
ECHO: I can't see the room. I can only see what it's still sending.
ECHO: That panel isn't in any of my records. Either copy.
ECHO: Which means someone put it there on purpose, and did not tell me. I find I'm pleased.
